ei.title: The Guardian of the Blue Heart of the Planet
ei.subject: 영어2

fullPassage: The Guardian of the Blue Heart of the Planet When most people were fascinated by the mysteries of exploring space, one remarkable individual appreciated the appeal of the ocean before many others, and eagerly explored the deep ocean. When people asked her, “Isn’t it scary down there?” she would reply, “What’s there to be afraid of? When I go down there, I delight in the life that I see.” Long before others, this person recognized that not only is the ocean full of life, but that it also needs to be protected. She is the legendary marine biologist named Sylvia Earle. Sylvia Earle was born in 1935 in New Jersey. Having moved to Florida at the age of twelve, she began exploring the beaches and observing the diverse marine life of the Gulf of Mexico. On her first birthday in Florida, her parents gifted her a pair of swimming goggles, perfect for someone who loved the ocean. Her father encouraged her, saying, “These will help you with your underwater explorations. Now all you have to do is dive in.” With her goggles, Earle gained a clearer view of the ocean’s wonders. At 17, she took her first deep dive, descending 10 meters in a lake wearing the diving suit that belonged to her friend’s father. Earle was thrilled to observe fish while breathing naturally underwater. As Earle experienced the excitement of diving, her desire to explore grew, and she eventually became one of the first marine scientists to use scuba equipment. Her innate sense of adventure and curiosity guided her academic journey, ultimately leading her to become a pioneer in ocean exploration and conservation. Sylvia Earle’s love for the ocean fueled her desire to explore further. In 1969, the same year astronauts first stepped on the moon, the Tektite Project allowed scientists to live in underwater habitats situated in the Virgin Islands. However, Earle was unable to participate in the project. “The people in charge just couldn’t cope with the idea of men and women living together underwater,” she said. The following year, having been chosen to lead the all female Tektite II Project, she spent two weeks living 15 meters beneath the ocean’s surface, along with four other oceanographers. She pushed the boundaries of underwater exploration and challenged gender stereotypes. Earle’s residence on the reef allowed her to observe and understand the complexities of the ecosystem. Her scientific findings were published, including the biology of coral reef fishes. The all female Tektite II crew became heroes upon their return to Earth’s surface, receiving attention similar to that of the astronauts’ historic moon landing. In 1979, Sylvia Earle accomplished a historic achievement off the coast of Oahu, Hawaii. Using the JIM suit, she dove 381 meters deep and walked on the ocean floor unattached for two hours. It was marked as the world’s deepest solo dive at that time. It earned her the title “Her Deepness.” As she descended, Earle was charmed by the glowing creatures that flashed like stars against the darkness. Among them were some species she had studied but never seen before, such as the deep sea squid that emits a glowing liquid to defend itself. During the dive, Earle planted a flag on the seafloor to symbolize the significance of ocean exploration in comparison to space exploration. She associated the moment with Neil Armstrong’s first steps on the moon and noted “These accomplishments had a few parallels. The modern world had two ‘final frontiers’ yet to explore: deep space and the deep ocean.” Her achievement in Hawaii was one small step towards the day when human beings would come to know and respect the vast world of life underwater. Earle was appointed the first female chief scientist at the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) in 1990. She aimed to shift NOAA’s focus from exploiting the ocean’s resources to prioritizing ocean research and conservation. Despite her efforts, Earle, as a senior official of the government, faced restrictions on her freedom of speech and action. Therefore, she resigned two years later to become a more active environmental activist. Returning to the private sector granted Earle the freedom to express herself. Through her work in science and technology businesses, public lectures, and writing books and articles for the mass media, Earle has been able to use her expertise and experience to campaign for the ocean’s conservation. Earle has committed herself to a lifetime of raising public awareness about the importance of the ocean. In 2009, her efforts gained prominence through three key events. She played an important role in initiating a global digital platform, which allows users to explore underwater worlds virtually, fostering appreciation for marine ecosystems. She was also awarded the TED Prize, a distinguished annual award that grants winners a wish to change the world, along with financial support. Earle’s wish was to create a global network of marine protected areas, or “Hope Spots,” which serve as refuges from pollution, overfishing, and other threats. Finally, this wish led her to establish Mission Blue, a non-profit organization that aims to inspire action to explore and protect the ocean. Since its establishment, protected ocean areas have increased from less than 1% in 2009 to approximately 8% in 2023. Mission Blue’s goal is to protect 30% of the ocean by 2030, in line with the International Union for Conservation of Nature’s recommended target for maintaining ocean health. For Earle, Mission Blue represents not only an organization, but also a movement, driven by a shared passion for the ocean and dedication to its preservation. As an oceanographer, author, and lecturer, she consistently inspires individuals to acknowledge the ocean’s significance. Earle said, “Since the 1980s, about half of the world’s coral reefs have disappeared. Ten percent of the sharks remain. They are not all gone. However, there is hope of preserving endangered marine species. There are more whales and turtles today than when I was young because most nations are protecting them from harm.” Although humans are largely responsible for many of the stresses on the ocean, Earle believes that we also have the power to ensure its survival. Earle reminds us of the importance of the ocean by saying, “If you think the ocean isn’t important, imagine Earth without it. No ocean, no life.” With over 7,000 hours underwater and more than 100 expeditions, Sylvia Earle has made significant contributions to the field of marine science. Her lifelong journey will undoubtedly continue to inspire future generations to protect and preserve the ocean, the blue heart of the planet.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.analysis:
① gained: 'With her goggles, Earle gained a clearer view'(고글로 Earle은 더 선명한 시야를 얻었다)는 과거의 일을 나타내는 과거동사라서 적절해요. ✅

② observing → observe: 여기가 정답(틀린 곳)! 'Earle was thrilled to ___ fish'(Earle은 물고기를 관찰하게 되어 몹시 신났다)에서 「be thrilled to+동사원형」 구조라 동사원형 observe가 맞아요. 현재분사 observing은 틀려요. ❌ ←정답

③ experienced: 'As Earle experienced the excitement of diving'(다이빙의 흥분을 경험하면서)에서 시간 부사절의 과거동사라 적절해요. ✅

④ leading: 'ultimately leading her to become a pioneer'(결국 그녀가 개척자가 되도록 이끌며)는 앞 내용을 부연하는 분사구문(-ing)이라 적절해요. ✅
det.tip: 감정을 나타내는 「be thrilled to+동사원형」 → was thrilled to observe.

det.korean: ③ choosing → chosen (having been + 과거분사, 완료 수동 분사구문)
det.analysis:
① stepped: 'the same year astronauts first stepped on the moon'(우주비행사들이 처음 달에 발을 디딘 바로 그해)에서 과거의 사실을 나타내는 과거동사라 적절해요. ✅

② participate: 'Earle was unable to participate in the project'(Earle은 그 프로젝트에 참여할 수 없었다)에서 「be unable to+동사원형」이라 원형 participate가 맞아요. ✅

③ choosing → chosen: 여기가 정답(틀린 곳)! 'having been ___ to lead the all female Tektite II Project'(전원 여성 팀을 이끌도록 선택되어)에서 그녀는 '선택을 받은' 대상이므로 「having been+과거분사」의 완료 수동 분사구문이 되어야 해요. been 뒤에는 과거분사 chosen이 맞고, choosing은 틀려요. ❌ ←정답

④ pushed: 'She pushed the boundaries of underwater exploration'(그녀는 수중 탐사의 한계를 밀어붙였다)에서 과거동사라 적절해요. ✅
det.tip: 「having been+과거분사」 완료 수동 분사구문: having been chosen(선택되어서).

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ③ driving → driven (수동 분사구문 — a movement는 추진되는 대상)
det.analysis:
① increased: 'protected ocean areas have increased'(보호 해역이 증가해 왔다)에서 「have+과거분사」의 현재완료라 increased가 적절해요. ✅

② maintaining: 'recommended target for maintaining ocean health'(해양 건강을 유지하기 위한 권고 목표)에서 전치사 for 뒤의 동명사라 maintaining이 적절해요. ✅

③ driving → driven: 여기가 정답(틀린 곳)! 'Mission Blue represents ... a movement, ___ by a shared passion'(공동의 열정에 의해 움직이는 하나의 운동)에서 movement는 열정에 의해 '추진되는' 대상이므로 수동의 과거분사 driven이 맞아요. 능동의 driving은 틀려요. ❌ ←정답

④ inspires: 'As an oceanographer, author, and lecturer, she consistently inspires individuals'(그녀는 꾸준히 사람들에게 영감을 준다)에서 3인칭 단수 주어 she에 맞춘 단수 동사 inspires가 적절해요. ✅
det.tip: 명사를 뒤에서 꾸미며 '~되는' 수동이면 과거분사: a movement driven by passion.

questions.passage: During the dive, Earle planted a flag on the seafloor to symbolize the ①<u>significance</u> of ocean exploration in comparison to space exploration. She aimed to shift NOAA’s focus from ④<u>exploiting</u> the ocean’s resources to prioritizing ocean research and conservation.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ② ignore → respect: 인류가 바다를 알고 '존중'하게 되는 날
det.analysis:
✅ ① significance: 'to symbolize the significance of ocean exploration'(해양 탐사의 중요성을 상징하기 위해) 문맥에 적절해요.

❌ ② ignore(무시하다) → respect(존중하다): 'the day when human beings would come to know and ___ the vast world of life underwater'(인류가 수중 생명 세계를 알고 존중하게 될 날)에서 흐름상 '존중하다(respect)'가 맞아요. '무시하다(ignore)'는 정반대라 부적절해요. ←정답

✅ ③ appointed: 'Earle was appointed the first female chief scientist'(최초의 여성 수석 과학자로 임명되었다) 문맥에 적절해요.

✅ ④ exploiting: 'from exploiting the ocean's resources'(해양 자원을 착취하는 것으로부터) 문맥에 적절해요.
det.tip: know and respect(알고 존중하다) ↔ ignore(무시하다)는 정반대 의미예요.

questions.passage: The following year, having been chosen to lead the all female Tektite II Project, she spent two weeks living 15 meters ①<u>beneath</u> the ocean’s surface, along with four other oceanographers.  She pushed the boundaries of underwater exploration and ②<u>reinforced</u> gender stereotypes.  Earle’s residence on the reef allowed her to observe and ③<u>understand</u> the complexities of the ecosystem. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① beneath: 'living 15 meters beneath the ocean's surface'(해수면 15미터 아래에서 생활하며) 문맥에 적절해요.

❌ ② reinforced(강화했다) → challenged(도전했다): 'She pushed the boundaries of underwater exploration and ___ gender stereotypes'에서 그녀는 전원 여성 팀을 이끌며 성별 고정관념을 '깨뜨리고 도전(challenged)'했어요. '강화했다(reinforced)'는 흐름과 정반대라 부적절해요. ←정답

✅ ③ understand: 'allowed her to observe and understand the complexities'(복잡성을 관찰하고 이해하도록 해 주었다) 문맥에 적절해요.

✅ ④ published: 'Her scientific findings were published'(그녀의 과학적 발견이 발표되었다) 문맥에 적절해요.
det.tip: 한계를 밀어붙이며 고정관념에 '도전'한 흐름 → challenged ↔ reinforced(강화).

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① protect and preserve(보호하고 지키다): 글 전체가 바다를 지키려는 Earle의 헌신을 다루고, 마지막 문장도 '미래 세대가 바다를 보호하고 지키도록 영감을 준다'로 마무리되므로 적절해요. ←정답

❌ ② exploit and abandon(착취하고 버리다): 바다를 지키자는 글의 주제와 정반대예요.

❌ ③ study and ignore(연구하고 무시하다): '무시하다'가 보존이라는 흐름과 어긋나요.

❌ ④ map and photograph(지도로 그리고 사진 찍다): 본문이 말하는 보존·보호의 핵심과 거리가 멀어요.
det.tip: 'the blue heart of the planet'을 지키려는 글 → protect and preserve the ocean.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 빈칸: raising public awareness(대중의 인식을 높이는 것)
det.analysis:
❌ ① selling marine products(해양 상품을 파는 것): 상업 판매는 본문 흐름과 무관해요.

❌ ② avoiding media attention(언론의 관심을 피하는 것): 그녀는 강연·집필·대중 매체로 적극 활동했으므로 반대예요.

❌ ③ building diving equipment(잠수 장비를 만드는 것): 장비 제작은 본문에 없어요.

✅ ④ raising public awareness(대중의 인식을 높이는 것): 뒤이어 디지털 플랫폼·TED·Mission Blue 등으로 바다의 중요성을 알린 활동이 이어지므로 적절해요. ←정답
det.tip: 바다의 중요성에 대한 '대중의 인식을 높이는 데' 평생을 바친 흐름이에요.

questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

det.analysis:
① 'Sylvia Earle was born in 1935'(1935년에 태어났다)와 일치해요.

② 'Having moved to Florida at the age of twelve, she began exploring the beaches'(열두 살에 플로리다로 이주한 뒤 해변을 탐험하기 시작했다)와 일치해요.

③ 'her parents gifted her a pair of swimming goggles'(부모님이 수영용 고글을 선물했다)와 일치해요.

❌ ④ 아버지는 'Now all you have to do is dive in'이라며 오히려 바다에 뛰어들라고 '격려(encouraged)'했어요. '말렸다'는 사실과 반대라 불일치예요. ←정답
det.tip: Her father encouraged her(아버지가 격려했다)를 확인하세요 — 말린 것이 아니에요.

ch: 그녀는 열두 살에 플로리다로 이주한 뒤 해변을 탐험하기 시작했다.
그녀의 부모님은 플로리다에서의 첫 생일에 수영용 고글을 선물해 주었다.
그녀의 아버지는 바다에 들어가지 말라고 그녀를 말렸다.

questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① 'Earle was unable to participate in the project'(1969년 참여 못 함) + 'having been chosen to lead the all female Tektite II Project'(이듬해 전원 여성 팀을 이끎)와 일치해요. ←정답

❌ ② 그녀는 '전원 여성(all female)' 팀과 '2주(two weeks)' 머물렀어요. 남성 동료·6개월은 틀려요.

❌ ③ 'Her scientific findings were published'(연구 성과가 발표되었다)와 반대예요.

ch: 그녀는 1969년 프로젝트에는 참여하지 못했지만, 이듬해 전원 여성으로 구성된 팀을 이끌었다.
그녀는 남성 동료들과 함께 6개월간 해저에 머물렀다.
그녀는 해저 생활 중 어떠한 연구 성과도 세상에 내놓지 못했다.
그녀는 깊은 바다가 위험하다고 판단해 탐사를 포기하였다.

❌ ④ 그녀는 'charmed by the glowing creatures'(빛나는 생물들에 매료되었다)라고 했어요. 어떤 생물도 못 본 채 돌아왔다는 것은 사실과 반대라 불일치예요. ←정답
det.tip: glowing creatures(빛나는 생물들)에 매료되었다는 문장을 확인하세요.

ch: 1979년 그녀는 하와이 앞바다에서 역사적인 업적을 이루었다.
그녀는 JIM 슈트를 입고 381미터 깊이까지 내려갔다.
이 잠수는 당시 세계에서 가장 깊은 단독 잠수로 기록되었다.
그녀는 해저에서 어떤 생물도 보지 못한 채 곧바로 되돌아왔다.

questions.passage: The Guardian of the Blue Heart of the Planet When most people were fascinated by the mysteries of exploring space, one remarkable individual appreciated the appeal of the ocean before many others, and eagerly explored the deep ocean.  When people asked her, “Isn’t it scary down there? ” she would reply, “What’s there to be afraid of?  When I go down there, I delight in the life that I see. ” Long before others, this person recognized that not only is the ocean full of life, but that it also needs to be protected.  She is the legendary marine biologist named Sylvia Earle.
questions.stem: 위 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① 도입부는 남들보다 먼저 바다의 매력을 알아보고 바다가 보호받아야 함을 깨달은 전설적 해양 생물학자를 소개하므로 글의 주제로 적절해요. ←정답

❌ ② 우주·해양 탐사의 기술 비교는 글의 중심이 아니에요.

❌ ③ 심해 생물의 발광 원리는 뒤에 잠깐 언급되는 소재일 뿐 주제가 아니에요.

❌ ④ 국제기구의 법적 규제 과정은 본문의 초점이 아니에요.
det.tip: 도입부가 한 인물(해양 생물학자)과 바다 보호를 강조한다는 점에 주목하세요.

ch: 바다의 가치를 일찍 알아보고 탐사와 보호에 헌신한 한 해양 생물학자
우주 탐사와 해양 탐사의 기술적 차이에 대한 비교 분석
심해 생물이 빛을 내는 원리와 그 생태학적 기능
해양 오염을 막기 위한 국제기구의 법적 규제 과정

questions.passage: Earle has committed herself to a lifetime of raising public awareness about the importance of the ocean.  In 2009, her efforts gained prominence through three key events.  She played an important role in initiating a global digital platform, which allows users to explore underwater worlds virtually, fostering appreciation for marine ecosystems.  She was also awarded the TED Prize, a distinguished annual award that grants winners a wish to change the world, along with financial support.  Earle’s wish was to create a global network of marine protected areas, or “Hope Spots,” which serve as refuges from pollution, overfishing, and other threats.  Finally, this wish led her to establish Mission Blue, a non-profit organization that aims to inspire action to explore and protect the ocean.  Since its establishment, protected ocean areas have increased from less than 1% in 2009 to approximately 8% in 2023.  Mission Blue’s goal is to protect 30% of the ocean by 2030, in line with the International Union for Conservation of Nature’s recommended target for maintaining ocean health.  For Earle, Mission Blue represents not only an organization, but also a movement, driven by a shared passion for the ocean and dedication to its preservation.  As an oceanographer, author, and lecturer, she consistently inspires individuals to acknowledge the ocean’s significance.
questions.stem: 위 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① Modern Deep-Sea Diving Suit Technology(현대 심해 잠수복 기술): 장비 기술은 글의 중심이 아니에요.

❌ ② How Space Exploration Beat Ocean Research(우주 탐사가 해양 연구를 이긴 방법): 본문은 둘을 대등하게 보며 우열을 말하지 않아요.

❌ ③ The Economic Upside of Overfishing(남획의 경제적 이점): 남획은 바다를 위협하는 요소로 제시되므로 반대예요.

✅ ④ A Lifelong Champion of the Ocean(바다를 지킨 평생의 투사): 강연·디지털 플랫폼·Mission Blue 등으로 바다를 탐험하고 지켜 온 그녀의 삶을 요약하므로 제목으로 적절해요. ←정답
det.tip: 강연·집필·Mission Blue로 바다를 탐험하고 지켜 온 삶을 포괄하는 제목을 고르세요.

ch: How Space Exploration Beat Ocean Research
A Lifelong Champion of the Ocean

questions.passage: Among them were some species she had studied but never seen before, such as the deep sea squid that emits a glowing liquid to defend itself.  During the dive, Earle planted a flag on the seafloor to symbolize the significance of ocean exploration in comparison to space exploration.  She associated the moment with Neil Armstrong’s first steps on the moon and noted “These accomplishments had a few parallels.  The modern world had two ‘<u>final frontiers</u>’ yet to explore: deep space and the deep ocean. ” Her achievement in Hawaii was one small step towards the day when human beings would come to know and respect the vast world of life underwater.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 표현이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
밑줄 바로 뒤 'yet to explore: deep space and the deep ocean'(아직 탐험해야 할 깊은 우주와 깊은 바다)이 단서예요.

❌ ① 버려진 공간: 탐험해야 할 대상이라는 흐름과 반대예요.

❌ ② 이미 다 밝혀진 분야: 아직 탐험이 남았다는 'yet to explore'와 모순돼요.

✅ ③ 인류가 아직 정복하지 못한 마지막 미지의 영역: 깊은 우주와 깊은 바다처럼 인류가 앞으로 탐험해야 할 미개척 영역을 뜻하므로 적절해요. ←정답

❌ ④ 물리적 경계선: 'frontier'를 단순한 경계로만 본 오해예요.
det.tip: 'yet to explore'(아직 탐험해야 할)가 밑줄 표현의 뜻을 알려 줘요.

ch: 더 이상 탐험할 가치가 남아 있지 않은 버려진 공간
과학자들이 이미 그 원리를 완전히 밝혀낸 연구 분야

questions.passage: It was marked as the world’s deepest solo dive at that time.  It earned her the title “Her Deepness. ” As she descended, Earle was charmed by the glowing creatures that flashed like stars against the darkness.  Among them were some species she had studied but never seen before, such as the deep sea squid that emits a glowing liquid to defend <u>itself</u>. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 대명사가 가리키는 대상으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
밑줄 친 itself는 바로 앞의 'the deep sea squid that emits a glowing liquid to defend itself'에 나와요.

✅ ① 발광 액체를 내뿜어 자신을 방어하는 심해 오징어: itself는 스스로를 방어하는 주체인 '심해 오징어(the deep sea squid)'를 가리키므로 적절해요. ←정답

❌ ② 깊은 바다의 어둠: 어둠은 방어하는 주체가 될 수 없어요.

❌ ③ 산호초 물고기: 이 문장의 주체가 아니에요.

❌ ④ 우주비행사들: 전혀 관련이 없어요.
det.tip: to defend itself(자신을 방어하기 위해)의 주체가 누구인지 바로 앞에서 찾으세요.

questions.passage: Earle was appointed the first female chief scientist at the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) in 1990.  She aimed to shift NOAA’s focus from exploiting the ocean’s resources to prioritizing __________.  Despite her efforts, Earle, as a senior official of the government, faced restrictions on her freedom of speech and action.  Therefore, she resigned two years later to become a more active environmental activist.  Returning to the private sector granted Earle the freedom to express herself.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 빈칸: ocean research and conservation(해양 연구와 보존)
det.analysis:
❌ ① resource extraction and sales(자원 채굴과 판매): 바로 앞 'exploiting the ocean's resources(자원 착취)'와 같은 방향이라 '~로 전환'이라는 대조 흐름에 맞지 않아요.

✅ ② ocean research and conservation(해양 연구와 보존): 'shift NOAA's focus from exploiting the ocean's resources to prioritizing ___'에서 '자원 착취'에서 벗어나 우선시할 대상은 '연구와 보존'이므로 적절해요. ←정답

❌ ③ military use and defense(군사적 이용과 방어): 본문에 없는 내용이에요.

❌ ④ tourism and entertainment(관광과 오락): 보존이라는 흐름과 어긋나요.
det.tip: from exploiting(착취로부터) → to prioritizing(우선시하는 쪽으로)의 대조를 보세요.

questions.passage: Earle said, “Since the 1980s, about half of the world’s coral reefs have disappeared.  __________.  They are not all gone.  However, there is hope of preserving endangered marine species.  There are more whales and turtles today than when I was young because most nations are protecting them from harm.
questions.stem:
위 글의 내용을 바탕으로, 다음 우리말에 맞도록 [조건]에 따라 영작하시오.

'상어의 10퍼센트가 남아 있다.'

[조건]
(1) of, percent, remain, sharks, Ten, the 를 모두 사용할 것
(2) 정확히 6단어로 쓸 것
(3) 영어로 쓸 것

det.korean: 부분을 나타내는 주어(Ten percent of ~)의 수 일치.
det.analysis:
구문 분석:
- 주어: Ten percent of the sharks(상어의 10퍼센트) — 「부분 + of + 명사」 형태의 주어예요.
- 동사: remain(남아 있다) — of 뒤 명사 sharks가 복수이므로 복수 동사 remain과 호응해요.
- 그래서 'Ten percent of the sharks remain' 순서가 돼요.
det.tip: 「부분(percent) of + 복수명사」는 of 뒤 명사에 동사를 맞춰요 → sharks remain.

questions.wa: Ten percent of the sharks remain
accept: Ten percent of the sharks remain

questions.passage: Earle’s residence on the reef allowed her to observe and understand the complexities of the ecosystem. Her scientific findings were __________ (publish), including the biology of coral reef fishes.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 흐름에 맞도록 괄호 안에 주어진 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (1단어, 영어로)

det.analysis: 구문 분석: 'Her scientific findings were ___ (publish)'에서 주어 findings(발견)는 발표를 '당하는' 대상이에요. be동사 were 뒤에서 수동태(be+과거분사)를 만들어야 하므로 publish의 과거분사 published를 써서 were published(발표되었다)가 돼요.
det.tip: 수동태 be + 과거분사: were published(발표되었다). publish → published.

questions.passage: It was marked as the world’s deepest solo dive at that time.  It earned her the title “Her Deepness. ” As she descended, Earle was charmed by the glowing creatures that flashed like stars against the darkness.  __________ but never seen before, such as the deep sea squid that emits a glowing liquid to defend itself. questions.stem:
위 글의 내용을 바탕으로, 다음 우리말에 맞도록 [조건]에 따라 영작하시오.

'그것들 중에는 그녀가 연구했던 몇몇 종들이 있었다.'

[조건]
(1) among, had, she, some, species, studied, them, were 를 모두 사용할 것
(2) 정확히 8단어로 쓸 것
(3) 영어로 쓸 것

det.korean: 장소·범위 부사구 도치 구문 + 생략된 관계절.
det.analysis:
구문 분석:
- Among them(그것들 중에는): 부사구가 문두로 나오면서 주어와 동사가 도치돼요.
- were some species(몇몇 종들이 있었다): 도치되어 「동사 + 주어」 어순이 돼요.
- (that) she had studied(그녀가 연구했던): species를 뒤에서 꾸미는, 목적격 관계대명사가 생략된 관계절이에요.
- 그래서 'Among them were some species she had studied' 순서가 돼요.
det.tip: 부사구(Among them)가 앞에 오면 「동사+주어」로 도치 → Among them were some species.

questions.wa: Among them were some species she had studied
accept: Among them were some species she had studied

questions.stem:
다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말이 되도록 주어진 단어를 올바른 순서로 배열하시오. (11단어, 영어로)

[ a / an / digital / global / important / in / initiating / platform / played / role / She ]

det.analysis:
구문 분석:
- She played an important role(그녀는 중요한 역할을 했다): 주어 + 과거동사 + 목적어.
- in initiating ...(~을 시작하는 데): 「play a role in+동명사」 구조라 전치사 in 뒤에 동명사 initiating이 와요.
- a global digital platform(세계적인 디지털 플랫폼): initiating의 목적어예요.
- 그래서 'She played an important role in initiating a global digital platform' 순서가 돼요.
det.tip: 「play a role in+동명사」: ~하는 데 역할을 하다 → a role in initiating.

questions.wa: She played an important role in initiating a global digital platform
accept: She played an important role in initiating a global digital platform
